name: Space Age pop product
region: Italy, Denmark, Finland, France and the United States
summary: The objects of the plastic age: chairs, lamps and tubs moulded in one piece from fibreglass, acrylic and ABS, with chrome and bright colour, in rounded forms that look like capsules, eggs and pods.

philosophy.core_thesis: The new plastics free the form: one mould makes a whole object in one piece, and its colour and curve show a hopeful, fast, technical future.
design_principles: Mould each major body in one piece, so that the object has no visible joint on its main surface.
Draw each body as a sphere, an egg, a pod or a tube with soft corners of 25 mm radius or more.
Give each object one saturated colour: orange, red, yellow, white or black, with a gloss finish.
Use chrome-plated steel for the stem, the base or the frame; keep it bright and thin.
Cut round holes or slots in a shell where the form needs light, air or a seat.
Show the object as a sculpture: it stands alone and looks good from every side.
Make each volume read as a capsule: round windows, round hatches and round buttons.
anti_patterns: Dark polished hardwood with a patina
Muted earth tones and natural linen

form.geometry: The sphere, the egg, the capsule, the tube and the pod, with a round hole as the main detail.
form.silhouette: A single smooth mass on a slim chrome stem or a low plinth, with no seam on the outline.
form.edges: Soft edges with a radius of 25 to 40 mm; no sharp corner on a body; the lip of a shell has a radius of 5 to 10 mm.
form.proportion: A pod chair is about 100 cm high and wide; a pendant globe is 30 to 50 cm in diameter; a stem is 3 to 5 cm thick.
form.ornament: None applied. The colour, the gloss and the round cut-outs give the surface its interest.
rules: Each body is one moulded piece with no more than one visible seam.
Each exterior corner has a radius of 25 mm or more.
Each object uses one bright colour on 80% or more of its surface.
Chrome covers less than 25% of the object and it carries the load.
A round or oval cut-out is the only surface detail.

materials.rule: Plastic makes about 70% of the visible surface; chrome and glass make most of the rest, and fabric appears only as a thin pad.

finish.gloss: 85–98 GU on moulded plastic and chrome; 10–40 GU only on glass and cloth
finish.patina: The style wants a new, bright and unmarked surface; a scratch or a yellow tint is a fault.

hardware.section: Stems and tubes 30–50 mm; a rail or a rod 10–16 mm
hardware.joints: One-piece mouldings; a chrome plate or a swivel bolt joins the shell to the base.
hardware.handles: A round hole in the body, a flush disc or a short chrome loop.
hardware.switches_and_taps: A large round push button or a flat disc rocker in coloured plastic; a chrome lever tap on a smooth cylinder.

palette.strategy: One saturated pop colour on each large body, with white or black as the second, and chrome as the neutral.

processes: hand lay-up of fibreglass in a mould
manufacture.scale: Studio mouldings of a few hundred pieces, then series of many thousand pieces from plastics and furniture firms.
manufacture.signs: A smooth shell without a seam on the face, a thin ridge where a mould halves meet, and a chrome swivel base.

objects.form: moulded pod bath on a plinth
large round push plate in bright plastic
modular boxes on a steel frame
hanging planter in the form of an egg

positive: studio product photograph, bright even light

evidence.title: Panton chair by Verner Panton, designed 1960

emotion.target_response: Playful optimism: the viewer sees a smooth, bright capsule and feels the excitement of a technical future.

use_cases: product briefs for plastic furniture reissues
a still life for a design museum shop
a prop list for a 1960s film set
avoid_when: The room needs warm, hand-made and natural objects.
The brief asks for a period revival in wood or brass.

modifiers.how: Keep the plastic, but split each body into laminate planes with loud patterns and angles.
Replace the capsule forms with grid-based boxes in matte grey and white plastic.
Swap fibreglass for bent beech and oak, and gloss for oil.

era_blend.note: A reissue keeps the style; a new object keeps only the one-piece mould and the colour.
